headline: Deloitte India deepens its CrowdStrike partnership
summary: Deloitte India expanded its global partnership with CrowdStrike to offer managed cybersecurity services built on the AI-native Falcon platform, aiming to help Indian enterprises consolidate tools and cut breakout-detection times.
angle: A case of consulting firms building alliance-led service lines (versus pure headcount-led delivery) to capture recurring managed-services revenue.

headline: Deloitte India expands CrowdStrike partnership for AI-era cybersecurity
summary: Deloitte India announced a local expansion of Deloitte's global CrowdStrike alliance, pairing the AI-native Falcon platform with its managed security services to help Indian clients counter AI-driven cyberattacks.
angle: Illustrates how consulting firms are bundling technology-vendor partnerships into service delivery.

headline: Deloitte India expands CrowdStrike partnership for AI-native cybersecurity
summary: Deloitte India expanded its global CrowdStrike partnership to pair the Falcon platform with Deloitte's managed security services, aimed at helping clients consolidate cybersecurity operations.
angle: A live example of how Big Four firms are bundling managed services on top of a tech vendor's platform to build recurring, AI-linked revenue streams.

headline: Deloitte India Expands CrowdStrike Partnership Into Managed Security Services
summary: Deloitte India announced on August 13, 2026 an expanded partnership with CrowdStrike to offer managed security services built on the Falcon platform, aimed at consolidating fragmented cybersecurity tooling for Indian clients.
angle: Why are Big 4 firms increasingly building recurring managed-service revenue lines (like security operations) on top of one-time advisory engagements?

headline: Deloitte India expands CrowdStrike partnership to modernize cybersecurity operations
summary: Deloitte India announced a local expansion of its global CrowdStrike alliance, building managed detection-and-response (MXDR) services on the AI-native Falcon platform for Indian enterprise clients.
angle: Illustrates how Big Four firms are building tech-alliance-led service lines (cybersecurity-as-a-service) rather than pure headcount-based consulting, relevant to "future of consulting business models" discussions.

headline: Google's Gemini 3.7 Flash undercuts rivals on price
summary: Google released Gemini 3.7 Flash on August 13, 2026, cutting introductory API pricing roughly in half versus its predecessor while lifting agentic-coding benchmark scores (DeepSWE v1.1 rose from 49% to 65.3%).
angle: Illustrates price-performance warfare in the AI model market and how cheaper, faster foundation models reshape product strategy for startups building on top of them — directly relevant to India's AI-native app ecosystem.

headline: India's trade deficit hits record even as exports scale new high
summary: India's merchandise exports rose 19.6% YoY to a record $44.24 billion in July, but the trade deficit still widened sharply as imports (led by crude oil) grew even faster, pushing the four-month FY27 deficit up 53% YoY.
angle: Good WAT/GD prompt: is rising export volume a false positive for 'Make in India' success when import-intensity of production is rising just as fast?

headline: India's trade deficit widens to six-month high of $32 billion
summary: India's July 2026 exports rose 19.6% YoY to a record $44.24 billion, but imports surged faster (17.5%) to $76.22 billion, pushing the trade deficit to a six-month high of $31.98 billion.
angle: Ties directly into currency (rupee) pressure, the US tariff/trade-deal backdrop, and whether record exports are being offset by an equally strong import bill — a solid macro WAT topic.

headline: Microsoft Begins Merging Copilot Apps Into a Unified 'Super App'
summary: Microsoft started consolidating Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, GitHub Copilot and its Autopilot agent layer into one app spanning consumer and commercial users, a plan Satya Nadella confirmed on Microsoft's July 29 earnings call.
angle: Product bundling/unbundling trade-off — what's gained and lost when four distinct products merge into one surface?

headline: Microsoft merges its two Copilot apps into one
summary: Microsoft began rolling out a single unified Copilot app that merges the consumer Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences across personal, work and school accounts, while confirming it will retire the Group Chat, Podcasts and Deep Research features starting August 18, 2026.
angle: Good prompt on product portfolio rationalization — why a company merges two competing product lines, the cost of sunsetting features users relied on, and bundling as a strategy against fragmented AI assistants.

headline: Microsoft merges its two Copilot apps into one, ahead of a "super app" push
summary: Microsoft began rolling out a unified Copilot app, merging the consumer and Microsoft 365 Copilot apps into one experience while keeping personal and work data separated.
angle: Why does maintaining two overlapping apps create user confusion and engineering overhead, and what risks must a PM manage when merging products?

headline: OpenAI Previews 'Ultrafast' Mode Running 14x Faster
summary: OpenAI previewed an Ultrafast mode for GPT-5.6 Sol on August 13, 2026, running at up to 14 times normal speed.
angle: Latency as a product feature — when does 'faster' change how and where an AI product gets used, not just how it feels?

headline: OpenAI previews a 14x-faster model tier
summary: OpenAI previewed "Ultrafast" mode for GPT-5.6 Sol, powered by Cerebras hardware, generating up to 750 tokens/second for latency-sensitive API workflows — currently in limited preview.
angle: Illustrates how PMs segment a single model into speed/cost/quality tiers for different customer workflows.

headline: Rupee slips to 95.40/USD as FII outflows and elevated crude weigh on the currency
summary: The rupee fell to 95.40/USD on continued FII selling and Brent crude near $87.89/barrel; the rupee has depreciated ~5% YTD, among the weakest major Asian currencies in 2026.
angle: Who wins and loses from a weaker rupee (IT/pharma exporters vs. oil importers/dollar-debt firms), and should RBI intervene?

headline: Auto-parts maker Jaya Hind Industries to invest Rs 600 crore in expansion
summary: Die-casting components maker Jaya Hind Industries announced a phased Rs 600-crore investment over two years to expand capacity at its Pune and Chennai plants, adding 12+ high-pressure die-casting machines and a new Chennai facility.
angle: A concrete mid-cap capex example for discussing how India's auto-component ecosystem is localising and scaling ahead of the EV transition.

headline: EY report: IT services M&A stayed resilient at $14.8B in H1 2026 as AI reshapes buyer priorities
summary: EY's H1 2026 deal-insights report found 449 IT-services M&A deals worth a disclosed $14.8 billion, broadly flat versus H1 2025, with AI pushing buyers toward targets with scale, sector depth and ecosystem strength (cloud, data/analytics, cybersecurity, managed services led activity).
angle: Gives candidates a data point for "how is AI changing consulting/IT-services M&A strategy" questions, showing dealmaking resilience despite softer discretionary tech spending.

headline: EY: IT services M&A hits 449 deals worth $14.8 billion in H1 2026 as AI reshapes buyer priorities
summary: EY's H1 2026 deal report finds IT services M&A activity held broadly steady on volume, with cloud, data/analytics and cybersecurity targets leading deal-making even as discretionary spending stays soft.
angle: Good material on how AI is shifting the rationale for M&A from pure scale to sector depth and ecosystem strength — a useful consulting/corp-strategy talking point.

headline: Gold rallies to $4,399/oz as rate-cut bets and central bank buying drive demand
summary: Gold rose to $4,399/oz driven by falling odds of further Fed hikes and continued central-bank buying; UBS projects a retest of $5,000 in H1 2027 (bank forecast, not fact).
angle: Connect record gold prices ahead of India's festive/wedding season to import-bill and current-account-deficit concerns — a recurring WAT theme.

headline: Google's "Made by Google" event pushes Gemini deeper into hardware and paid tiers
summary: Google unveiled Pixel 11 with Gemini-powered features, a Pixel Tag tracker, and a tiered AI subscription ladder from $4.99 to $199.99 bundling Google Home Premium and YouTube Premium.
angle: Is bundling AI features into premium subscription tiers genuine ambient-computing value or primarily an upsell/lock-in play, and how would a PM measure the difference?

headline: India's management consulting market set to nearly double to $17 billion by 2031
summary: India's management consulting market is estimated at roughly $9.4 billion in 2026 and is projected to grow about 12.7% annually to reach $17 billion by 2031, with MBB firms running large India offices and BCG India alone fielding 460+ consultants.
angle: Useful market-sizing context for 'why consulting, why now in India' questions, and to discuss what's fueling demand (govt digitisation, GenAI advisory, PE-led diligence).

headline: India’s retail inflation hits a 19-month high
summary: India’s CPI inflation rose to 4.45% in July 2026, up from 4.38% in June and the highest reading in 19 months, driven by rising food and energy prices linked to the Middle East conflict’s impact on crude and the rupee.
angle: Directly feeds the RBI rate-hike debate — candidates should connect inflation data to the central bank’s next policy move.

headline: Klook launches global AI-generated brand platform across 15 markets
summary: Klook and BBH Singapore unveiled a new global brand platform using an AI production system generating thousands of localized visual assets tuned to local travel trends.
angle: Discuss the tension between letting AI generate near-infinite localized creative variants and holding one coherent brand identity across 15 markets.

headline: Molbio Diagnostics IPO subscribed 70x as investors chase India's primary market boom
summary: Molbio Diagnostics' Rs 939.7-crore IPO was subscribed 70.27x; grey market premium implied a listing price near Rs 953, roughly 18% over the upper price band.
angle: Does 70x oversubscription reflect genuine confidence in Molbio's diagnostics platform, or momentum-chasing in India's 2026 IPO wave?

headline: Nifty IT slides as AI-automation fears and Accenture's guidance cut spook investors
summary: TCS, Infosys and HCL Tech fell up to 2% after Accenture cut FY26 revenue guidance to 3-4%, fueling worries AI adoption will shrink outsourcing demand; Nifty IT trades near 16x forward earnings vs Accenture's 10x.
angle: Argue whether Indian IT's valuation premium is justified given AI-driven demand risk, and what pivot each major IT firm needs to defend margins.

headline: Shiprocket's ₹1,617-crore IPO opens, testing appetite for loss-making enablement platforms
summary: E-commerce enablement platform Shiprocket opened its IPO despite a consolidated net loss of ₹79.24 crore on ₹2,024 crore revenue for FY26.
angle: How should a PM at a maturing B2B SaaS/logistics-enablement platform prioritize unit economics and monetization features as it approaches public markets?

headline: Tata Motors Q1 FY27: consolidated profit up 83%, standalone up just 8%
summary: Tata Motors posted consolidated net profit of Rs 2,560 crore (up 83% YoY); standalone CV business profit was Rs 1,528 crore (up 8%) on revenue up 23% and CV volumes up 26%.
angle: Explain the gap between the 83% consolidated jump and 8% standalone growth — which subsidiary is carrying the group, and what that implies about relying on one segment.

headline: Tata Motors' margins slip even as sales jump
summary: Tata Motors' Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 23% year-on-year, but EBITDA margin fell 60 bps to 11.7% as commodity costs bit into profitability.
angle: Good case for "growth vs. margin" trade-off discussions in auto/manufacturing finance.

headline: Tata Sons chairman Chandrasekaran to step down, reopening succession crisis
summary: N. Chandrasekaran announced he will exit as Tata Sons chairman when his term ends in February 2027, after months of boardroom deadlock over his reappointment.
angle: How does a leadership vacuum at the holding-company level threaten execution of Tata's ~$120B capex plan across semiconductors, aviation and EVs?

headline: US inflation cools to 3.4% in July, keeping September Fed rate-cut bets alive
summary: US CPI rose 3.4% YoY in July (down from 3.5%); core CPI rose 2.5% YoY, reinforcing market expectations of a Fed rate cut at the September FOMC meeting.
angle: How would a Fed rate cut transmit to India — cheaper dollar funding and FII inflows, versus a stronger case for RBI to hold given above-target inflation?

headline: Blinkit dark store's food licence suspended in Mumbai over hygiene violations
summary: Maharashtra's FDA suspended a Blinkit dark store's food licence in Malad, Mumbai after finding cockroach infestations, expired stock, and failure to follow FIFO/FEFO norms.
angle: How should a PM at a quick-commerce company balance dark-store expansion speed against building scalable, auditable quality/trust-and-safety systems?

headline: ChatGPT ads go global, land in five new markets
summary: OpenAI expanded its ChatGPT ad pilot beyond the US to the UK, Mexico, Brazil, Japan and South Korea from August 11, showing ads only to logged-in free-tier users while keeping paid subscription tiers ad-free.
angle: A global analogy for how AI chat interfaces are becoming a new advertising and discovery channel, useful for discussing the future of search-driven marketing in India.

headline: Danube Group explains its Bigg Boss 19 branded-entertainment bet
summary: Dubai developer Danube Group built a "Danube Apartment" into the Bigg Boss 19 house, rather than running a conventional logo sponsorship, to sell real estate to Indian/NRI buyers.
angle: Argue whether branded entertainment can move a high-ticket purchase like real estate the way it moves impulse categories.

headline: Deloitte tells the government to rethink import duties
summary: Deloitte India's latest Economic Outlook projects 6.5-6.8% FY27 GDP growth and urges the government to rationalise customs duties and reform Special Economic Zones ahead of the Budget.
angle: Shows how Big Four economic research becomes direct policy input — a good example of a consulting firm's advisory "product."

headline: FMCG giants pour more ad money into quick commerce
summary: Nestle India raised ad spend over 40% YoY in Q1 FY27 while HUL spent roughly Rs 1,657 crore on advertising and promotions in the June quarter, as FMCG majors rebalance brand-building against growing visibility demands on Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart.
angle: A strong prompt on how retail/commerce media is disrupting traditional ATL budget allocation for large FMCG advertisers.

headline: Global port congestion update: Felixstowe omissions, Hormuz risk, Guinea storage crunch
summary: Carriers are skipping calls at UK's Felixstowe due to congestion, maritime risk remains elevated in the Strait of Hormuz, and Guinea's Conakry port faces ~13.6-day waits from limited storage.
angle: Contrast two system responses to congestion — rerouting around a constrained node versus a chokepoint with no reroute option — for a discussion on network resilience.

headline: Govt directive bans "tip for a faster ride" prompts on Uber, Ola, Rapido
summary: Following an MoRTH crackdown, aggregators covered under the Motor Vehicles Act were directed to stop repeated tipping and add-on prompts, after a survey found 78% of users faced pop-ups even after declining.
angle: A sharp prompt on dark patterns in product design — where does persuasive UX end and manipulative UX begin, and how should PMs self-regulate before the regulator steps in?

headline: India's Russian crude imports hit a record for a second straight month
summary: India's purchases of Russian crude rose to a fresh record in July for the second consecutive month, even as refiners navigate Western sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil.
angle: A recurring favourite — sourcing strategy under geopolitical constraint, and how refiners balance cost, compliance and energy security.

headline: L&T joins the race to build rare-earth magnets in India, chasing a government incentive
summary: L&T is preparing to bid for India's Rs 7,280 crore incentive scheme to build domestic rare-earth magnet capacity, as China's ~90% grip on global magnet production threatens EV/electronics production.
angle: A response to single-source dependency risk — why subsidize capacity creation rather than just diversifying suppliers, given the lead time and technology gap?

headline: McKinsey: India's chemicals industry to nearly double to $255 billion by 2030
summary: McKinsey projects India's chemicals sector growing from ~$160B to $230-255B by 2030 (8-9% CAGR), led by eight arenas including semiconductors, EVs/batteries and renewables.

headline: OpenAI widens its ChatGPT ad experiment
summary: OpenAI expanded its ChatGPT ads test — shown only to logged-in Free/Go tier users — to the UK, Mexico, Brazil, Japan and South Korea, after starting in the US earlier in 2026.
angle: A textbook monetization-vs-user-experience trade-off for a PM to reason through, including why ads are tier-gated.

headline: SBI Research pegs India's Q1 FY27 GDP growth at 8%, a point above RBI's forecast
summary: SBI Research's nowcasting model projects 8% Q1 FY27 GDP growth vs. RBI's 7%, citing 24.1% YoY passenger vehicle growth and capex running at 27.8% of budget estimates.

headline: Swiggy agrees to refund restaurants as boycott deadline pushed to September

angle: A clean two-sided-marketplace conflict on platform commission and fee transparency versus supply-side trust.

headline: Toyota recalls over 508,000 Camry Hybrids for a two-year-old software defect
summary: Toyota is recalling 508,354 Camry Hybrids after a software initialization error disabled instrument clusters and turn signals; the intermittent fault took regulators two years to confirm.

headline: US court dismisses fraud case against Gautam Adani days before MSCI review
summary: A US federal court dismissed with prejudice the DOJ's securities-fraud indictment against Gautam Adani, Sagar Adani and a former Adani Green CEO, just before MSCI's quarterly index review.

headline: Air India will restore most flights it cut this summer over fuel costs and airspace curbs
summary: Air India will restore most of the 145 weekly international flights and ~20-22% of domestic capacity it suspended over record jet fuel prices and airspace restrictions, from September 1.
angle: A case of reactive capacity throttling in response to volatile input costs — could proactive network/fuel-hedging planning have avoided blanket route suspensions?

headline: Blackstone's Safe Harbor to buy MarineMax for $1.5 billion
summary: Blackstone-owned marina operator Safe Harbor agreed to acquire boat retailer MarineMax at a roughly 96% premium, merging marina infrastructure with retail, brokerage and financing.

headline: Cadbury Celebrations refreshes its Raksha Bandhan gifting range
summary: Cadbury Celebrations, with Ogilvy India, launched '#ThisTakraarIsSweet' alongside a redesigned premium gifting portfolio spanning Rs 100 to Rs 575 price points.
angle: Discuss how a legacy chocolate-gifting category defends share against modern D2C gifting brands by widening its price architecture.

headline: Doctors demand a watershed ban on junk food ads to children
summary: Over 30 doctors urged the health ministry to ban HFSS food advertising 6am-11pm, mandate warning labels, and bar sales in school canteens.
angle: Form a point of view on whether FMCG/QSR brands should get ahead of this with voluntary reformulation, or resist it — and what that signals about trading category growth for trust.

headline: IES Holdings to acquire structural-steel platform DBM Global for $650 million
summary: IES Holdings agreed to buy DBM Global, a structural-steel fabrication and industrial-services platform, creating a new "Structural" business line alongside its existing segments.
angle: Does adding an adjacent-but-distinct construction vertical smooth cyclicality across IES's portfolio, or is it "diworsification" that stretches management focus?

headline: IFC bets ₹225 crore on India's warehousing gap
summary: The International Finance Corporation will invest ₹225 crore in NDR Smart Spaces to build about 20 million sq ft of Grade-A dry and cold-storage warehousing across 14 tier-2/3 Indian cities.
angle: Highlights the logistics infrastructure gap in smaller Indian cities and why global capital is chasing it now.

headline: India gets its first standalone ammonia import terminal
summary: Aegis Logistics commissioned a 36,000-tonne ammonia storage terminal at Pipavav Port, backed by a 15-year take-or-pay agreement with Hindustan Zinc to feed a new fertiliser plant.
angle: A concrete example of long-term offtake contracts de-risking infrastructure investment — useful for supply-chain and capex questions.

headline: Mahindra Group consolidates real estate, hospitality under new CSO
summary: Mahindra Group named Shveta Arya (outgoing MD of Cummins India) as Group Chief Strategy Officer effective September 15, while consolidating its Mahindra Lifespace (real estate) and Mahindra Holidays (hospitality) businesses into a single strategic vertical led by Amit Kumar Sinha.
angle: A textbook conglomerate-portfolio-strategy case — bundling secondary 'growth gem' businesses under focused leadership to unlock capital and operational synergies, useful for discussing diversified Indian business group strategy.

headline: Meta open-sources Muse Glimmer, a 30B-parameter on-device AI model
summary: Meta released Muse Glimmer, an Apache 2.0-licensed 30-billion-parameter multimodal model designed to run locally on a single consumer GPU, positioning itself against OpenAI and Anthropic's closed offerings.
angle: A strong prompt on open-source vs. closed AI models as a platform strategy to compete on developer distribution.

headline: Shah Rukh Khan fronts Google's Gemini campaign for "Bharat"
summary: Google India launched a multilingual Gemini campaign starring Shah Rukh Khan, developed with McCann India, aimed at India's ~470 million Tier 2/3 internet users.
angle: Explain why a global AI brand borrows a legacy Bollywood icon's trust equity, rather than a digital-native creator, to cross the language barrier into non-metro India.

headline: Teledyne to acquire X-ray imaging maker Varex Imaging for $1.1 billion
summary: Teledyne agreed to buy Varex Imaging, adding X-ray tubes and photon-counting detectors to its digital-imaging portfolio, citing largely non-overlapping product lines.
angle: Is the acquirer's "limited overlap" framing a strength (true capability adjacency) or a red flag (thin synergy case)?

headline: US judge dismisses DOJ's bribery case against Gautam Adani, but criticizes DOJ's conduct
summary: A Brooklyn federal judge granted the DOJ's own request to drop the bribery indictment against Adani, but called the DOJ's reasoning "concerning" and kept charges against five co-defendants.

headline: Vodafone Idea narrows Q1 loss, posts first subscriber gain since merger
summary: Vodafone Idea cut its Q1 FY27 net loss to ₹3,754 crore as revenue rose 6% and ARPU climbed to ₹195, its first quarter of positive net subscriber additions since the merger.

headline: India plans a PLI scheme for polysilicon to plug a gap in its solar supply chain
summary: A planned PLI scheme targets 10+ GW of domestic polysilicon capacity; India has built 200+ GW of module and 32+ GW of cell capacity but remains import-dependent on upstream polysilicon.
angle: A capacity mismatch across a value chain — why does backward integration matter more than headline downstream capacity numbers?

headline: OpenAI shuts down its standalone Atlas browser, folds features into ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI's Atlas browser, launched October 2025, was retired on August 9, 2026, with its browser-agent capabilities absorbed into ChatGPT itself.
angle: When should a PM kill a standalone product surface rather than keep investing in it — what signals justify folding a feature back into the core platform?

headline: A US Senate Russia-sanctions bill could expose Indian exports to 100% tariffs

angle: A sourcing decision made for cost efficiency (cheap Russian crude) created concentrated geopolitical exposure across an unrelated value chain — discuss supplier concentration risk beyond cost/lead time.

headline: Ola Electric's Q1 FY27 turnaround leans on operating discipline, not just volume
summary: Ola Electric's deliveries nearly doubled sequentially to ~39,200 units and market share rose to 8.4%, while operating expenses fell 22%, aided by in-house 4680 cell production.
angle: Discuss how a manufacturer converts capacity utilization gains from vertical integration into margin rather than just top-line growth.

headline: Sarla Aviation gets India's first eVTOL design approval, clearing path to air taxis

headline: Airbus and Boeing stuck a decade from unblocking their composite-curing bottleneck

headline: Amazon, Flipkart, Myntra open Independence Day sale season
summary: Amazon's Great Freedom Festival and Flipkart's Freedom Sale launched with up to 80-90% off and bank-card tie-ups, ahead of Myntra's Aug 12-18 sale window.
angle: Discuss whether stacking sale calendars onto every national holiday erodes discount-led acquisition's long-term defensibility versus brand loyalty.

headline: ASCI finds 98% of summer ad claims failed compliance
summary: ASCI's "The Heat Is On" report reviewed 40 summer-season ads across sunscreens, coolers, air purifiers, personal care and wearables, and found 39 required correction or withdrawal for unsubstantiated claims.
angle: Be ready to argue whether claims-heavy seasonal advertising is a rational bet on short attention spans, or a trust liability once a regulator starts publishing violator rates by category.

headline: Dentsu Names India Its Top APAC Growth Market
summary: Dentsu Group reported India as its single biggest growth market across Asia-Pacific in H1 FY2026, as global ad holding companies rebalance investment toward the market.
angle: Why is India outgrowing the rest of APAC for global ad agencies right now — what's actually driving the spend (digital, e-commerce, D2C)?

headline: Government Readies a Dedicated PLI Scheme for Polysilicon
summary: The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy is developing a new PLI scheme to support over 10 GW of domestic polysilicon manufacturing — the key upstream raw material for solar cells and semiconductor chips.

headline: India's last-mile delivery boom is outrunning its B2B logistics backbone
summary: Quick-commerce dark stores scaled ~48% YoY to 5,000+ locations, but the upstream B2B logistics layer connecting factories, warehouses and distributors remains manual and fragmented.
angle: A Theory-of-Constraints trap — explain why optimizing the visible bottleneck (last-mile) without fixing the upstream flow doesn't raise system throughput.

headline: KKR-backed LEAP India opens Rs 2,480-crore IPO, heavy on offer-for-sale
summary: LEAP India's IPO comprised a Rs 480-crore fresh issue and ~Rs 2,000-crore offer-for-sale (~80% of issue size) at a price band of Rs 151-159.

headline: RBI's draft ban on revolving credit erases Rs 55,000 crore from Bajaj group in a day
summary: RBI's draft norms propose banning revolving/flexi-credit products for most NBFCs; Bajaj Finance and Bajaj Finserv shares fell ~6% and ~4%, wiping out roughly Rs 55,000 crore in combined market value.

headline: YouTube to Count Views From the First Frame

headline: Nielsen to acquire ad-verification firm DoubleVerify for $2.15 billion
summary: Nielsen agreed to buy DoubleVerify, combining audience measurement with ad-verification and brand-safety data into a single platform expected to generate over $4B in combined revenue.
angle: Does combined measurement-plus-verification data create real switching costs for advertisers, or could rivals replicate the value through partnerships instead of a merger?

headline: PhonePe expands into fixed deposits and daily micro-savings, deepening its super-app bet
summary: PhonePe launched fixed deposit distribution with partner banks/NBFCs and a Daily Recurring Deposit product starting at Rs 100/day.
angle: Weigh distribution-led adjacent expansion (aggregating partner FDs) against the risk of diluting the core payments use case.

headline: Punt Creative wins PizzaExpress India’s communications mandate
summary: Punt Creative was appointed as PizzaExpress India’s communications agency following a competitive multi-agency pitch, taking charge of digital strategy, social media, content and integrated campaigns.
angle: Useful for agency-client pitch dynamics and how QSR/casual-dining brands build digital-first engagement in India.

headline: RBI to Pilot India's First Polymer ₹10 and ₹20 Notes
summary: Governor Sanjay Malhotra confirmed a pilot of polymer currency notes beginning FY28 (1 billion pieces each of ₹10 and ₹20), with a tender for polymer substrate sheets closing August 18, 2026.
angle: Currency-management economics — why pilot cautiously rather than switch India's whole note supply to more durable polymer at once?

headline: WhatsApp starts testing age verification for Indian users ahead of DPDP Act rollout
summary: WhatsApp began testing a feature in India asking users to confirm date of birth, aimed at identifying under-18 users to comply with the DPDP Act's parental-consent requirements.
angle: How does a PM design a low-friction compliance feature like age-gating without tanking activation/signup conversion?

headline: WhatsApp tests age verification for Indian users
summary: WhatsApp began testing a feature asking users in India to submit their date of birth, getting ahead of upcoming Indian laws that require platforms to verify user age.
angle: A good prompt on compliance-driven product roadmaps — building a feature not for engagement but to pre-empt regulation in your largest market.

headline: Kim Kardashian’s SKIMS enters India via exclusive Reliance Brands tie-up
summary: Reliance Brands Limited signed an exclusive partnership to launch SKIMS, the shapewear and loungewear label co-founded by Kim Kardashian, in India — starting with stores in Delhi and Mumbai across physical and digital channels.
angle: A good prompt on market-entry strategy for global celebrity-founded brands — why a local-partner model over a standalone launch in India.

headline: Kim Kardashian's SKIMS enters India via Reliance
summary: Reliance Brands signed an exclusive partnership to launch SKIMS in India, opening first stores in Delhi and Mumbai as part of a phased retail and digital rollout.
angle: A classic market-entry case — why a global brand licenses distribution to a local conglomerate instead of going direct.

headline: Manipal Health Enterprises lists at 11% premium in India's second-largest 2026 IPO
summary: Manipal Health Enterprises' ₹9,275-crore IPO debuted at an 11% premium over its issue price, taking its market cap to roughly ₹77,600 crore despite muted retail demand.
angle: A good case to discuss IPO pricing and valuation of healthcare assets, and why institutional demand outpaced retail enthusiasm.

headline: North Central Railway's freight loading jumps 7.6%
summary: North Central Railway's freight loading rose 7.6% year-on-year to 7.24 million tonnes in April-July FY27, with the Prayagraj division up 30% on surging foodgrain and cement volumes.
angle: A live data point for "how is Indian Railways improving freight efficiency" — relevant to logistics and modal-shift discussions.

headline: RBI holds rates, raises growth forecast
summary: The RBI's MPC kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in its August review while raising India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 6.7%, even as CPI inflation ticked up to 4.4%.
angle: Core "explain the current monetary policy stance" question — neutral stance, inflation above target but growth resilient.

headline: RBI Holds Repo Rate at 5.25% for a Fourth Straight Meeting
summary: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee unanimously kept the repo rate at 5.25% and its stance 'Neutral', while raising the FY26 GDP growth forecast to 6.7% even as June inflation crossed the 4% target for the first time in 17 months.
angle: Classic WAT/GD prompt — why hold rates instead of cutting or hiking when growth is 'resilient' but inflation is turning up?

headline: RBI holds repo rate at 5.25% for fourth straight meeting, lifts FY27 growth forecast to 6.7%
summary: The RBI's MPC unanimously kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25% in its August policy review, while raising India's GDP growth projection to 6.7% on resilient domestic demand and robust exports.
angle: Staple GD/PI topic — link a "neutral" policy stance with June's above-target inflation print and the growth-inflation trade-off the RBI is managing.

headline: RBI proposes harmonised interest-rate framework across regulated entities
summary: The RBI proposed standardising how banks and NBFCs set and disclose interest rates on advances, aiming for greater transparency in loan pricing and stronger monetary transmission.
angle: Useful for questions on monetary policy transmission — why uniform pricing rules help rate cuts actually reach borrowers faster.

headline: RBI proposes on-tap licensing for Urban Co-operative Banks after a 20-year pause
summary: The RBI will issue draft guidelines allowing eligible credit cooperatives (minimum ₹10,000 crore deposits, 12% CRAR) to apply for fresh UCB licences year-round, ending a near two-decade freeze.
angle: Tests understanding of financial inclusion versus systemic risk — why the RBI paused UCB licensing after the PMC Bank crisis and what safeguards justify reopening it now.

headline: RBI to reopen cooperative bank licensing after 20 years
summary: The RBI will issue draft guidelines for "on-tap" licensing of Urban Cooperative Banks, requiring a minimum ₹10,000 crore deposit base, ending a pause that has held since 2004.
angle: Tests understanding of financial-sector consolidation and why regulators gate entry into banking.

headline: Flipkart times food-delivery entry to Bengaluru restaurants' boycott of Swiggy and Zomato
summary: Flipkart is launching food delivery in Bengaluru via ONDC at a 10-11% restaurant commission, as local restaurants threaten to stop accepting Swiggy/Zomato orders over 24-25% commissions.
angle: How does a new entrant exploit supply-side dissatisfaction and existing platform assets to disrupt an incumbent's commission-based business model?

headline: Rapido's Zero-Commission 'Ownly' Grabs Early Share From Swiggy-Zomato
summary: Rapido's flat-fee food-delivery product Ownly has scaled to over 40,000 orders across 25,000 restaurants in Bengaluru, capturing an estimated 7-10% of the market within months.
angle: Pricing-model innovation (flat fee vs. commission) as the core product lever for winning restaurant supply in a two-sided market.

headline: Maruti Suzuki posts highest-ever monthly production as new Gujarat plant ramps up
summary: Maruti Suzuki produced a record 248,845 units in July 2026, up 33% year-on-year, as its new Plant D at Hansalpur pushed total manufacturing capacity to 29 lakh units annually.
angle: Good for capacity-planning questions — how phased plant commissioning helps a manufacturer match a demand upswing without overbuilding.

headline: 15% Surcharge on Newspaper Ads Takes Effect
summary: A surcharge mandated by the Indian Newspaper Society added 15% to the cost of print advertising from August 1, 2026, pushing brands and agencies to rework media-spend plans.
angle: Good prompt on media-mix reallocation — would you defend or cut print spend as costs rise even as circulation keeps declining?

headline: GST tightens the e-way bill net
summary: From August 1, GSTN made the "Ship-to GSTIN" field mandatory in e-Invoice and e-Way Bill APIs whenever shipping details differ from the billing party, closing a compliance gap in multi-location dispatches.
angle: A practical example of how tax-compliance plumbing changes ripple into daily logistics and dispatch operations.

headline: GSTN Tightens E-Invoice and E-Way Bill Validation Rules
summary: From August 1, 2026, GSTN made the Ship-to GSTIN field mandatory in e-Invoice and e-Way Bill API validations whenever Ship-to information is present, tightening compliance checks on interstate goods movement.
angle: Operations-compliance intersection — how must ERP and logistics systems adapt when tax authorities tighten invoice-level validation for shipments?

headline: India's Factory PMI Slips to a 4½-Year Low
summary: India's manufacturing PMI fell to its weakest reading in four-and-a-half years, even as the government keeps expanding PLI-driven capacity.
angle: Tension between long-term capacity building ('Make in India') and near-term order softness — what operational levers would you pull first?

headline: McKinsey names a new country boss for Germany and Austria
summary: McKinsey appointed Andreas Venus as Managing Partner for Germany and Austria from August 1, succeeding Fabian Billing, who moves to the firm's global Shareholders Council.
angle: A window into how partnerships handle leadership succession — relevant if asked about the consulting firm ownership/governance model.

headline: Ola Electric Registrations Nearly Double Quarter-on-Quarter
summary: Ola Electric registered 16,144 vehicles in June 2026, continuing a recovery in production and delivery after well-publicized quality and service issues.
angle: What operational fixes (supply chain, service network, QC) typically underlie a turnaround like this, and how would you verify it's durable?

headline: SEBI's New Mutual Fund Rules Force a Scheme Name-Portfolio Match
summary: Under SEBI's Mutual Funds Regulations 2026 (effective April 1), fund houses had a roughly six-month window, running into August 2026, to ensure scheme names accurately reflect what they actually invest in, alongside stricter cost-disclosure norms.
angle: Investor protection vs. innovation trade-off — does forcing stricter naming/categorization limit a fund house's ability to launch niche products?

headline: Maruti Suzuki's volumes surge, but profitability cracks
summary: Maruti Suzuki's Q1 FY27 volumes grew 29.3% year-on-year to 682,724 units, yet EBITDA margin fell sharply to 8.6% from 12.6%, dragging the stock down.
angle: Pairs well with Tata Motors as a sector-wide story on how top-line growth can mask margin erosion.

headline: Flipkart adds Pay Later across its entire app family
summary: Flipkart, partnering with PayU Finance, launched “Flipkart Pay Later” with Pay Later, Pay-in-3 and EMI options — live simultaneously across Flipkart, Myntra and Flipkart Minutes.
angle: Tests cross-platform feature rollout strategy — how a single credit product gets embedded across a company’s entire app portfolio to lift conversion.

headline: Google gives robots a “high-level brain”
summary: Google DeepMind launched Gemini Robotics ER 2, an embodied-reasoning model that processes video, language and sensor data to plan multi-step tasks and coordinate multiple robots, now live in preview on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
angle: A live example of the “reasoning model + action model” split in agentic AI product architecture — useful for any AI-PM system-design discussion.

headline: Tata Motors to Launch Four New EVs in 12-18 Months
summary: Chairman N Chandrasekaran confirmed new-generation Nexon, Altroz and Tigor EVs are coming, with the premium Avinya brand to follow later.
angle: How should an incumbent auto major sequence plant retooling and multiple EV model launches off one shared manufacturing base?

headline: PwC: Indian manufacturers back AI for growth but lag China on innovation
summary: A PwC study of 443 industrial manufacturers finds 59% of Indian firms see AI as key to strategic goals, yet only 16% anchor strategy in product leadership, versus 63% of Chinese peers.
angle: Great for a consulting-style "so what": strong AI adoption doesn't automatically translate into strategic differentiation — candidates can discuss the gap between tool adoption and capability building.

headline: PwC: Indian manufacturers embrace AI but lag China on innovation
summary: A PwC study of 51 Indian and 51 Chinese manufacturers found 59% of Indian firms see AI as core to their five-year strategy, yet only 16% anchor strategy in product leadership versus 63% in China — a gap PwC says could cap margins and export sophistication.
angle: Rich material for “India vs China manufacturing” GD prompts — Indian firms adopt AI for customer-facing use cases, China for shop-floor efficiency and product innovation.

headline: Tata Motors' Sanand plants hit by Gujarat floods, supplier network disrupted
summary: Torrential rain (300-500mm in 24 hours) and flooding in Gujarat halted production at Tata Motors' Sanand plants (Nexon, Tiago, Tigor, Sierra) and disrupted several component suppliers, with recovery underway.
angle: A textbook case for single-location manufacturing risk and multi-tier supplier resilience planning in operations strategy.

headline: Amazon India ships AI seller assistant, built on Bedrock, Nova and Claude, to 1.7 million sellers
summary: Amazon rolled out a 24/7 AI assistant (in English and Hinglish) that helps its 1.7 million India sellers with listings, pricing and global expansion, cutting listing errors by 10% and operational effort by 70%.
angle: A strong case for AI-feature ROI — how a PM would define and measure success metrics (error rate, effort reduction) for an agentic AI feature at marketplace scale.

headline: PhonePe launches SmartPages, an AI page-builder for merchants
summary: PhonePe introduced SmartPages inside its Payment Gateway dashboard, letting merchants describe their product in plain language, including vernacular, and have AI generate a ready-to-use payment page.
angle: Useful to discuss cutting merchant onboarding friction as a growth lever for a payments platform, and vernacular AI as a product differentiator in India.

headline: Welspun One to nearly double its warehousing footprint
summary: Warehousing developer Welspun One plans to lease over 10 million sq ft of industrial and logistics space over the next three years, betting on continued demand from e-commerce, manufacturers and 3PL operators.
angle: A good example of capacity-planning and expansion strategy riding India’s logistics realty boom.

headline: Port congestion exposes cracks in India’s logistics chain
summary: Cargo backlogs at Nhava Sheva and Mundra ports were driven not by vessel or terminal capacity but by shortages of trailers, drivers and diesel for inland evacuation — exposing weak links in India’s freight network beyond the port gate.
angle: A sharp case for discussing where India’s logistics bottleneck really sits — rarely the port itself, but the inland supply chain feeding it.

headline: McKinsey Plans to Cut ~10% of Its Workforce as AI Hits Back-Office Roles
summary: McKinsey is planning to cut roughly 10% of staff in non-client-facing roles — back-office functions, junior research and support — over the next 12-18 months, as generative AI compresses delivery timelines.
angle: The advisor becomes the advised — what does it say about the consulting model that AI is now reshaping the firms that sell AI transformation to everyone else?

headline: Deloitte: Indian Enterprises Lead Global Peers in At-Scale AI Adoption
summary: A Deloitte report found Indian enterprises deploying AI at scale most strongly in product development (62%), strategy & operations (56%), marketing & sales (55%) and supply chain (48%), ahead of the global average.
angle: If India is ahead on AI adoption by function, where specifically should a consulting engagement add value beyond the technology itself?

headline: BCG Tops IIM Ahmedabad's 2026 Placements as Finance and Consulting Lead Hiring
summary: At IIM Ahmedabad's PGP final placements (February 2026), Boston Consulting Group was the largest recruiter with 33 offers in the first cluster alone, as finance and consulting firms dominated hiring across a 100%-placed batch.
angle: Why does consulting keep winning the recruiting race at top B-schools even as the industry talks about AI-driven headcount cuts?

headline: PwC frames a $550 billion AI opportunity for India
summary: PwC India’s “AI Edge for Viksit Bharat” framework estimates AI could add $550 billion in value across agriculture, healthcare, energy, education and manufacturing by 2035, built on real pilots like AI-driven TB detection and smart metering.
angle: Useful for macro/GD questions on AI-and-development — moving the conversation from productivity buzzwords to sector-specific, India-relevant economic modelling.

headline: Consulting keeps winning the campus placement race at IIMs
summary: IIM Bangalore's 2026 summer placements saw consulting offers jump to a record 46% of the batch, led by Accenture Strategy, BCG, Bain and McKinsey; IIM Ahmedabad's final placements showed BCG (33), McKinsey (21) and Bain (20) as top recruiters.
angle: Directly relevant to the reader's own placement prospects — shows which firms are hiring most aggressively right now.
